headline: Mbappe's penalty sends France to World Cup quarterfinals after 1-0 win over Paraguay
summary: Kylian Mbappe scored from the spot in the 70th minute, breaking down a resilient Paraguay side in a hard-fought last-16 clash. France will now face Morocco in the quarterfinals.
details: France secured a 1-0 victory over a stubborn Paraguay in a niggly World Cup last-16 match in Philadelphia. Kylian Mbappe converted a penalty in the 70th minute, ensuring France's progression to the quarterfinals. The game was played in sweltering 38-degree Celsius heat.

Paraguay, ranked 41st in the world, had previously eliminated Germany on penalties and aimed for another upset. They employed a defensive strategy with a back five, frustrating France's attacking efforts for much of the game.

Despite France dominating possession, they struggled to create clear chances against Paraguay's low block. It wasn't an attacking masterclass from Les Bleus, who were restricted to long-range shots for long spells.

The breakthrough came after Desire Doue, a second-half substitute, was fouled in the box by Diego Gomez. Mbappe calmly slotted the penalty, marking his seventh goal of the tournament and putting him level with Lionel Messi as joint-top scorer.

Mbappe's individual brilliance continues as he now has 19 World Cup goals in 19 appearances, just one shy of Messi's overall record. France will now prepare to face Morocco in the quarterfinal clash in Foxborough next Thursday.
